rules: All holder dictionaries below are copied exactly from accepted C01 research (docs/campaign-certification/C01/research/brazil.json, packets C01-34 and C01-43). Grouping them under an existing person ID does not promote dates, prove a tenure or extend an office.

Point observations are never expanded to full terms. No start or end is inferred from a successor, election, convention, leave, return or death report beyond what the accepted holder dictionary itself states (Brizola's until 2004-06-21 is the only accepted end).

Requested windows are appearance intervals from the CLAUDE-C06-BRAZIL-01 handoff table with exclusive ends. Where a bound comes from party_leaders.json, leadership production, the cutoff, a batch split or unaccepted C01 research rather than accepted research, the person entry says so.
Real history stops at 2026-09-07; every window in this batch ends on or before 2026-09-08 (exclusive).

Image dates describe the source photograph, never the appearance window. Every age gap and every artistic extension (standing body, hands, trousers, shoes, completion of a hidden crown) is declared in the prompt and here.

Likeness references are dated photographs of the exact person whose licence string, as stated by Commons extmetadata, matches FREE_LICENSES exactly. Ported licences such as 'CC BY 3.0 br', NC/ND terms, agency or press photos, TV stills and unversioned grants are rejected. Original bytes and metadata stay outside Git; the repository copy is byte-identical. Nothing was cropped, edited or labelled; crops happen at registration.

Claude generates, edits and labels no image. Codex renders with its built-in image tool from the exact prompt files and input order in render-request-batch-01.md and returns the unchanged outputs; Claude then performs and records the identity, likeness, era and visual review. No review flag is true yet.
Each review batch contains at most ten people.
HTTP response header captures that contain the client IP address or GeoIP cookies are never copied, cited, hashed or committed.

Prompt sha256 values are over the LF bytes committed to Git (equal to `git show HEAD:<path> | sha256sum`). No .gitattributes rule covers these files yet, so a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true writes CRLF bytes; that hash is recorded beside each pin.

Ages use the registry birth dates in party_leaders.json (Temer 1940-09-23, Baleia Rossi 1972-06-09, Lupi 1957-03-16, Brizola 1922-11-22, which conflicts with other sources). Birth dates are not accepted C01 research.

Birth date sources disagree (see birth_date_evidence): on 22 January 1922 he is 72 at the window start, 76 in the photograph and 82 at the end; on the registry's 22 November 1922 he is 72, 75 and 81. The prompt asks for a man in his mid-seventies, as in the photograph, and states '72 when this appearance begins and 81 or 82 when it ends'. The reference is a side profile and the hat hides his forehead and crown, so the receding swept-back crown is a declared artistic completion; a research-only 1280 px thumbnail of the rejected 2002 photograph (File:Niemeyer e Brizola.jpg) was viewed to confirm the bareheaded swept-back gray hair and uncovered ears. It is not shipped and not a generation input. The suit, white shirt, burgundy tie and standing body are artistic; the white collar and dark sleeve follow the photograph.
